text: AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness（DSH Web 插件）：将兼容 AI 网关接入 DSH，为每个网关建立独立模型提供方。它探测并读取模型目录，支持 OpenAI Chat、OpenAI Responses、Anthropic Messages 和 Gemini 协议；用户可管理多个网关、隐藏模型、编辑模型参数、测试模型并查看受支持后端的配额。适合希望在 DSH 中统一使用自建或第三方网关的人。需要提供网关地址和 API Key，密钥由 DSH credentials 服务保存。

AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness connects compatible gateways to DSH. It supports OpenAI Chat, Responses, Anthropic Messages, and Gemini. Users can manage gateways, hide models, edit parameters, test models, and view quota data. A gateway address and API key are required.

DSH 怎么配置多个 OpenAI 兼容服务地址？
想在模型列表里管理不同网关提供的模型
能不能为某个模型改上游名称和上下文参数？
我想测试网关上的模型能否正常响应
在 DSH 对话里使用 Anthropic 或 Gemini 协议的网关
I want to connect my compatible AI gateway to DSH.
How can I manage models from several gateways in one DSH instance?
AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness 的功能「多网关接入」：在设置页保存多个兼容网关；每个网关在模型选择器中独立分组。可先测试连接再保存。 通过网关设置页或模型管理操作触发，结果用于配置和检查模型。
AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness 的功能「模型目录与参数管理」：读取网关模型目录，并可发现、隐藏模型或编辑协议、上下文、输出上限和推理能力等覆盖项。 通过网关设置页或模型管理操作触发，结果用于配置和检查模型。
AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness 的功能「模型连通性测试」：用户可对单个模型或一批模型发起小型请求测试，查看协议、耗时、响应预览及分类后的错误结果。 通过网关设置页或模型管理操作触发，结果用于配置和检查模型。

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ai-gateway-provider)
[](LICENSE)

Connect **any AI gateway** to DeepSeek Harness — chat over OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini protocols, with models, parameters and quota in one place.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness：Most providers are the same three endpoints with different names on the box. Instead of a list of supported vendors, this plugin follows the protocol and probes each gateway for what it can actually do: if it speaks `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`, it works — including a gateway nobody has heard of yet.
dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Install：```sh

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · in DeepSeek Harness → Settings → Plugins → install by package name：dsh-ai-gateway-provider
```

Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.1-rc.1 and < 0.3.0. This README describes **0.7.2**; the version npm actually serves is whatever `npm view dsh-ai-gateway-provider version` reports (0.7.1 when this was written), and that result is the one to trust. Existing screenshots are illustrative and may predate the current editor.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · What it does：- **Probe before saving.** A gateway is written only after it lists its models with the address and token you entered. A wrong URL or a revoked token is refused at that moment, not on the first message.
- **Several gateways at once.** Every saved gateway gets its own provider route and stays usable; the chat model picker groups them by gateway name, so two gateways serving the same model id never collide.
- **Model management per gateway.** Fetch the gateway's list, add a model it does not list, edit any model's name, upstream mapping, context window, output cap, input modalities, reasoning levels and wire protocol, and hide what you do not want.
- **Grouped model table.** Models are grouped by vendor — `devin/claude-opus-5` and `claude-opus-5-5` sit together under Anthropic — with a per-group "tested / working" count. Groups collapse, and the grouping can be switched off.
- **Hide models.** Hide one model, or a whole vendor group, from the chat picker without removing it; Hidden models stay in the list, greyed out, so clicking again unhides them. Hiding never turns an automatic gateway into a fixed list.
- **Shelve a gateway.** The eye
dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Supported backends：The plugin never needs to recognise a vendor — recognition only decides the icon and which quota endpoint to call.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Supported backends：| Backend | Detected by | Quota |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New API / one-api / done-hub / one-hub / Veloera / VoAPI | `GET /api/status` (`system_name`, `quota_per_unit`) | `GET /api/usage/token/` |
| LiteLLM | `GET /key/info` answering | key budget (`spend` / `max_budget`) |
| CLIProxyAPI | `GET /` banner `CLI Proxy API Server` | none |
| Anything else that is OpenAI-compatible | `GET /v1/models` answering | none |

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Supported backends：Wire protocols per model: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini. The gateway's `supported_endpoint_types` decides; the model editor can override.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Several gateways, one picker：Each saved gateway is registered as its own provider route, so every gateway is usable at the same time — there is nothing to switch between. The model picker groups models by gateway, and the group heading is the gateway's name: two gateways serving the same model id appear as separate rows instead of one shadowing the other.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Several gateways, one picker：Routes are assigned once and persisted with the gateway list, so editing or deleting one gateway never shifts another's route. The first gateway keeps the legacy route id `ai-gateway` and later gateways derive their own (`ai-gateway-<slug>`), which is why conversations recorded before 0.7.0 still resolve to the gateway they used.

New conversations choose a model like any other provider; after that each conversation remembers its own choice.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Hiding a gateway：The eye button on a gateway card hides that gateway from the conversation model picker. Hiding is reversible and local to the picker: the address, token, per-model settings and history resolution all stay, and the gateway is not asked for quota while hidden. Everything else keeps working — test connection, model tests, model editing and the capability page. Press the same button to bring its models back.
dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Hiding a gateway：Hiding is not deletion: use the card's delete action when the configuration itself should go.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Viewing a gateway：There is no "active" gateway to select. The old `activeChannel` value in the config is ignored, and the page no longer has an activate action: every saved gateway is always registered and always usable in chat.

Clicking a row in the gateway list is a viewing action only. It changes which gateway the detail summary and the **Model capabilities** page describe, and nothing else — chat availability is decided per conversation by the model you pick, not by the row you last clicked.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Add or edit a gateway：1. Settings → AI Gateway → **Add gateway**. The address field is focused for a new gateway.
2. Once the address is a valid `http(s)` URL, a **Fetch info** button appears inline in the address field. It reads public endpoints only — `/api/status`, the site's home page and its favicon: no token is read or sent, and no model is called. It reports the gateway type, its version, the site title, a suggested name and the icon.
3. The suggested name is filled in only while the name field is empty; a name you typed is never overwritten.
4. Enter the token and press **Test connection** to see the model counts, then Save.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Add or edit a gateway：Saving still probes the gateway with the real token; the fetch-info button is a preview, not the save check.

Tokens live in the DSH credential store — never in the config, never returned to the page.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Performance：Opening the settings page reads no model catalog. The page snapshot carries the gateway list, site identities and quota instead of model entries, so switching tabs or leaving the page open does not fan out model-list requests to every gateway. A gateway's model list is loaded on demand, when you open that gateway (`models/list` for the selected gateway), and the periodic refresh no longer triggers catalog reads.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Model capabilities and controls：**Sync data** reloads the currently viewed gateway's model capabilities even when no settings changed. **Fetch models** also refreshes that gateway's capabilities after discovery, including in automatic mode when every discovered model is already enabled. Neither action requires reopening settings; periodic background snapshots still do not fetch model catalogs.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Model capabilities and controls：Fetching a model list also resolves per-model reasoning levels and speed tiers. Reasoning resolution prefers manual mappings, then gateway `supported_reasoning_levels` / `default_reasoning_level`, then pi-ai's bundled catalog or family defaults. Those fallbacks are model metadata, **not gateway declarations**; unrecognised support remains unknown. `supports_reasoning_effort_updates` only says whether a running turn may change its level (Claude answers `false`), so it never blanks the level selector. A resolved model also keeps pi-ai's own `compat` block for that id (for example `forceAdaptiveThinking`), so a level reaches the upstream as an adaptive effort rather than a thinking-token budget. Only per-model `service_tiers` / `supported_service_tiers` establish speed declarations. Discovery never sends billed model probes.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Model capabilities and controls：The model editor has independent reasoning and speed switches, with row-based add/remove controls and editable API values. Turning speed off hides the composer control and omits `service_tier`, including old conversation choices. Turning reasoning selection off removes its level menu. Detection metadata is retained for re-enabling.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：Each speed row maps a local selector id to a wire `service_tier`. Presets are Standard → `default`, Fast → `priority`, Ultrafast → `ultrafast`. Edit their wire values or choose Custom tier, e.g. `turbo` → `vendor-priority`. When all detected tiers are present, Add creates a custom row. These per-model/per-gateway mappings persist as `allowedServiceTiers` and `serviceTierMap`; OpenAI Chat / Responses requests send the mapped wire value. There is no model-default speed dropdown: choose a tier in the conversation.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：[OpenAI's Fast mode guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode) documents `fast` and `priority` as equivalent request spellings; the plugin canonicalises `fast` to `priority` when comparing declarations and response stamps. [Ultrafast mode](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ultrafast-mode) has model and availability restrictions: its presence as an editor preset does not make it available on every model, account or gateway.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：**Switching in a conversation**: when the current model is an AI Gateway GPT model with speed enabled and per-model declared, response-stamped, or explicitly configured tier evidence, a *⚡ Speed* button appears left of the model button in the composer. It selects preset or custom tiers for **this conversation**, and the menu labels each tier's evidence. The choice applies to this model in this conversation only; other conversations retain their existing model configuration; adding a custom row does not automatically select it. (DSH's model menu has no extension row for plugins, so the control sits beside it.)
dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：**How support is decided** — per gateway and model, with three kinds of evidence kept apart:

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：| Evidence | Source | Shown as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway declaration | per-model `service_tiers` / `supported_service_tiers` in the gateway catalog (CLIProxyAPI serves it at `/v1/models?client_version=`) | declared tiers in the editor, options marked *declared* |
| Response stamp | **Test** sends one tiny request with the tier and reads the returned `service_tier` | ✓ matching stamp (UI: *in effect*) / ↓ different stamp / ? no stamp |
| Manual configuration | explicitly configured local-to-wire mapping, not declared or confirmed by a matching response stamp | *Configured* in the composer menu, with the actual wire value in its tooltip |

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：Speed support is checked for the exact gateway and upstream model, using its selected OpenAI Chat / Responses protocol. A GPT name only limits this feature's scope; neither names, gateway brands nor models.dev prove speed support. An explicitly empty declaration means "no accelerated tier declared"; absent metadata means unknown. Labels describe declarations, response stamps or manual configuration—not independent proof that the upstream actually accelerated the request. Lower latency is not proof either.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · GPT / OpenAI speed tiers：**Per gateway**:
- **CLIProxyAPI** declares tiers in its client catalog (Codex-backed GPT models usually declare Fast).
- **New API** deployments may filter `service_tier` unless the channel allows passthrough; a differing or missing response stamp is not by itself a diagnosis of where filtering occurred.
- **Other gateways** remain usable through the generic OpenAI-compatible path. Missing tier declarations stay unknown; manual mappings are optional trials, not detected support.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Model tests：One tiny request per model (or per batch), with a very small output cap. Results record the protocol, latency, an output preview and a classified error (no channel, bad token, rate limited, timed out). All four wire protocols are supported: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages and Gemini.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Model tests：The Gemini test uses exactly the chat URL — `POST {gateway}/v1beta/models/{model}:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` with `x-goog-api-key` — and requires a `finishReason`; a bare `[DONE]`, or an OpenAI-shaped stream, is not a Gemini success. The Gemini chat path is built on the same `/v1beta` base, so a gateway that works in chat answers the test the same way.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Boundaries：- **No automatic paid probing.** Connection checks, the fetch-info button and catalog reads send read-only requests and never call a model.
- **User-triggered actions do call models.** Model tests (including batch tests) and chat itself are real requests and may be billed. Only you start them.
- **A response stamp is not independent proof.** A returned `service_tier` records what the gateway reported; it does not prove the upstream really accelerated the request, and shorter latency does not prove it either.
- **Not in scope:** Claude or Gemini **speed tiers** (where such modes exist). Their **protocols** are supported for chat and model tests; only the OpenAI Chat / Responses speed tiers are.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Privacy and safety：- Requests are read-only `GET`s; **no model is called and nothing is billed** by probing.
- Redirects are never followed, so a token cannot be forwarded to another host.
- Site icons are fetched only from the gateway's own origin, size-limited, and cached on disk for 24 hours.
- Identification uses only public endpoints and stores only public facts (family, version, title, icon) — no token, no user data.
- A gateway without a quota endpoint is reported as having none, never as an error.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Limits：- No image or video generation tools: the New API tools in `dsh-newapi-provider` depend on its own task API. A gateway's image models are listed but not driven from here.
- Quota adapters cover the three families above. A backend that exposes quota some other way shows none until an adapter is added.
- Gateway identification is heuristic; a gateway that hides every public endpoint is treated as a plain OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which is still enough to use it.

dsh-ai-gateway-provider README · Development：```sh
npm test                                    # 154 tests against local fake gateways
node scripts/probe.mjs --base <url>         # probe from a shell
GATEWAY_KEY=sk-... node scripts/probe.mjs --base <url>
```
